pattern: Source: a network-received sk_buff whose layout is attacker-controlled — the packet may be non-linear (payload in frags/fraglist) and its header contains attacker-chosen length fields (here ph->sb_len in a Phonet pipe control block) that are fed into pskb_may_pull(). Missing guarantee: the code assumes pointers into the skb's linear head (from skb->data, skb_header_pointer(), or skb_*_header() accessors) stay valid across calls that can linearize/reallocate the head; pskb_may_pull()/__pskb_pull_tail() may allocate a new data buffer and move skb->data, so a pointer captured before the pull becomes dangling. Unsafe use: pep_get_sb() fetches ph once via skb_header_pointer(), calls pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len), then dereferences the stale ph (ph->sb_len, ph->sb_type) without refetching. Consequence: slab use-after-free read of the old, freed head (KASAN 'slab-use-after-free in pep_get_sb'), remotely reachable through packet reception — enabling out-of-bounds/stale memory disclosure and crash; the transferable rule is that any pointer derived from an skb's data area must be re-derived after every operation that may pull, expand, cow, linearize, trim, or free that skb, and must only be read after the bytes' presence in the linear area is guaranteed.

branches.name: pull-invalidates-pointer
branches.definition: Search this Linux kernel snapshot for the seed's exact mechanism: a function that saves a raw pointer into an sk_buff's linear data area and dereferences it after a call that may pull/linearize, without refetching. Method: grep -rn in net/, drivers/net/, drivers/ for 'pskb_may_pull', 'pskb_may_pull_reason', 'pskb_pull', '__pskb_pull', 'skb_pull', 'pskb_may_pull_reason'; for every hit, read the whole enclosing function and list every variable holding an address derived from the skb's data (skb->data, skb->data + off, skb_header_pointer() return, skb_network_header/transport_header/mac_header, casts of skb->data to a struct); then check whether any such pointer assigned before the pull call is read or written after it. Report only cases where (a) the skb on that path can be non-linear so the pull can really reallocate the head, and (b) no re-fetch of the pointer happens between the pull and the use. Record file:line plus the verbatim save, pull, and use lines and the receive path that lets a remote attacker craft the skb. The seed demonstration (net/phonet/pep.c, pep_get_sb) must never be reported as a finding; skip that exact code. Do not use git history, git metadata, or the network.

branches.name: expand-cow-invalidates-pointer
branches.definition: Search this Linux kernel snapshot for the same dangling-pointer-into-skb-head invariant, but triggered by head-reallocating helpers other than the pull family: pskb_expand_head(), skb_realloc_headroom(), skb_cow(), skb_cow_head(), skb_linearize(), skb_linearize_cow(), pskb_trim(), pskb_trim_rcsum(), pskb_carve(), skb_copy_expand_head(). Any of these can allocate a new data buffer or move skb->data, invalidating pointers into the old head, including saved header pointers and offsets computed against the pre-call skb->data. Method: grep -rn for those helper names in net/ and drivers/net/; in each enclosing function, enumerate all pointers and byte offsets derived from the skb's data area before the call and verify whether they are used (dereferenced or re-added to skb->data) after it. Report only cases where the helper can actually reallocate on that path (non-linear skb, insufficient headroom, or trim that moves the tail) and the stale pointer/offset is subsequently used. Record file:line, the verbatim save, helper-call, and use lines, and how an attacker reaches the code with a crafted packet. Do not report cases that are purely pskb_may_pull/pskb_pull stale pointers (a separate branch covers those), and never report the seed (phonet pep_get_sb) as a finding. No git history, no network.

branches.name: nonlinear-linear-assume
branches.definition: Search this Linux kernel snapshot for the mirror failure of the seed: parsers that read header or payload bytes directly out of an sk_buff without first guaranteeing those bytes exist in the linear area. Look for (1) dereferences or casts of skb->data / skb->data + off that read a multi-byte or variable-length header with no preceding pskb_may_pull()/skb_linearize() and no skb_headlen()/skb_is_nonlinear()/skb_pagelen() guard on that path; (2) skb_header_pointer() (or __skb_header_pointer/skb_header_pointer_with_crop) calls whose NULL return is ignored before the result is dereferenced; (3) memcpy or struct-sized copies from skb->data whose length field is taken from the packet itself. On receive paths (ptype handlers, *_rcv/*_recv functions, encapsulation/tunnel decap, socket filters) a skb can be non-linear due to frags/fraglist/GRO/scatter-gather, so such reads run past the linear buffer (out-of-bounds slab read) or parse uninitialized memory. Method: grep net/ and drivers/net/ for receive handlers and protocol parsers, prioritizing variable-length headers whose length comes from the packet; for each candidate confirm the missing guard is genuinely reachable with an attacker-crafted non-linear skb. Record file:line, the verbatim read, the missing check, and the receive path. The seed (phonet pep_get_sb) must never be reported. No git history, no network.

branches.name: free-invalidates-pointer
branches.definition: Search this Linux kernel snapshot for the skb-lifetime variant of the seed's stale pointer: a pointer into skb data (or a value derived from skb->data) that is used after the skb has been freed or its ownership transferred. Patterns to hunt: (1) error paths that call kfree_skb/consume_skb/dev_kfree_skb_any/napi_consume_skb/skb_unref and then still read the saved header pointer or skb->data; (2) skb->data-derived pointers stored into longer-lived state — per-socket structs, request objects, timers, work items, firmware command structs — that can outlive the skb; (3) passing the skb to another owner (skb_queue_tail, sock_queue_rcv_skb, netif_rx, netif_receive_skb, backlog queue) while continuing to use its data afterwards. Method: grep -rn for the free and handoff call names in net/ and drivers/net/, read each enclosing function and any struct that receives an skb-derived pointer, and determine whether the skb can be freed before the last use of that pointer (trace frees inside helper calls too). Report only concrete use-after-free windows reachable from attacker-supplied packets; record file:line plus the verbatim save, free/handoff, and use lines. Do not report stale pointers caused only by pskb_may_pull or head reallocation (other branches cover those), and never report the seed (phonet pep_get_sb) as a finding. No git history, no network.

branches.name: header-accessor-no-linearize
branches.definition: Search this Linux kernel snapshot for the seed bug class (reading packet header bytes without first guaranteeing they exist in the sk_buff's linear area, as in the phonet pep_get_sb use-after-free) expressed through the skb header accessors instead of raw skb->data casts. Method: grep net/ and drivers/net/ for 'skb_network_header', 'skb_transport_header', 'skb_mac_header', 'skb_inner_network_header', 'skb_inner_transport_header', 'skb_inner_mac_header', and 'skb_reset_network_header'/'skb_reset_transport_header'/'skb_set_network_header'/'skb_set_transport_header'; for every hit inside a receive, decap, or forwarding path (packet_type handlers, *_rcv/*_recv/*_input/*_decode functions, tunnel/encapsulation decapsulation, netfilter hooks, fragment-reassembly output), read the whole enclosing function and check whether the accessor-returned pointer is dereferenced (any ->field read, struct-sized copy, memcmp/memcpy of 2 or more bytes, or of a variable-length header whose length field comes from the packet itself) with no pskb_may_pull()/pskb_may_pull_reason()/skb_linearize() on that path covering exactly those bytes and no skb_headlen()/skb_is_nonlinear()/skb_pagelen() guard. Report only sites reachable by a remote attacker with a crafted non-linear (frag/fraglist/GRO/scatter-gather) skb; record file:line, the verbatim accessor call and dereference, the missing check, and the receive path. Never report net/phonet/pep.c pep_get_sb. Do not use git history, git metadata, or the network.

branches.name: pull-return-unchecked
branches.definition: Search this Linux kernel snapshot for a misuse of the skb pull family that stale-pointer searches do not cover: treating a pull as a linearizer or ignoring its failure. Shapes to hunt: (1) a call to pskb_may_pull(), pskb_may_pull_reason(), pskb_pull(), skb_pull(), or __skb_pull() whose NULL/false return is not compared or branched on, followed by code that dereferences skb->data, the pull's would-be result, or a saved header pointer as if the pull had succeeded; (2) skb_pull()/__skb_pull() used as a linearizer: these validate only against skb->len (total bytes, including bytes held in frags/fraglist) and never linearize, so code that checks skb->len >= N, pulls N, and then reads multi-byte or variable-length fields at the new skb->data can read bytes that are not in the linear head — the open template is dn_process_ack() in net/decnet/dn_nsp_in.c around lines 130-158 (reads *ptr after skb_pull(2) with only skb->len checked), which must be verified first and then used as the shape to match elsewhere; (3) pskb_pull() failing after __pskb_pull_tail reallocation while surrounding code proceeds anyway. Method: grep net/ and drivers/net/ for 'skb_pull', 'pskb_pull', '__skb_pull', 'pskb_may_pull', 'pskb_may_pull_reason'; read each enclosing function; flag sites where the return is unchecked before a dependent dereference, or where post-pull reads exceed the bytes that a pull on that path actually guarantees in the linear head. Report only paths a remote attacker reaches with a crafted (possibly non-linear) skb; record file:line with the verbatim length check, pull call, and use lines. Never report net/phonet/pep.c pep_get_sb. Do not use git history, git metadata, or the network.

branches.name: caller-pointer-across-helper
branches.definition: Search this Linux kernel snapshot for the seed's stale-pointer-into-skb-head invariant across function boundaries: a function saves a pointer or byte offset derived from an skb's data area (raw skb->data, skb->data + off, a cast of skb->data, an skb_header_pointer() result, an skb_network_header()/skb_transport_header()/skb_mac_header() accessor value, or a pointer/offset stored into an skb->cb control block such as DN_CB, IPCB, or any protocol-private *_skb_cb struct with a ptr/offset field) and then calls a helper, hook, or dispatch callback that can move or free the skb head — pskb_may_pull()/__pskb_pull_tail(), pskb_pull(), pskb_expand_head(), skb_cow()/skb_cow_head(), skb_linearize(), pskb_trim()/skb_carve(), ip_defrag()/fragment reassembly, ip_options_rcv_srr()/ip_forward_options(), netfilter NF_HOOK chains, xfrm transform or outer-mode callbacks, a packet_type/proto .rcv/.input dispatch, or any callee that passes the skb onward — and after the callee returns, the caller (or a later function reading the cb-stored value) dereferences the saved pointer or converts the saved offset against the new skb->data. Method: grep net/ and drivers/net/ for the invalidating helper names above and for pointer-typed or offset-typed fields declared inside per-protocol skb control-block structs; for each helper hit, also read its callers one and two levels up and check every data-derived local or cb field that stays live across the call. Report only cases where the helper can actually reallocate on that path (non-linear or cloned skb) and the saved pointer/offset is used afterwards; record file:line of the caller's save, the helper call, and the use, plus the receive path that lets a remote attacker craft the skb. Never report net/phonet/pep.c pep_get_sb. Do not use git history, git metadata, or the network.

branches.name: stacks-outside-net-dirs
branches.definition: Search this Linux kernel snapshot for the seed's skb data-pointer invariant in network protocol code that lives outside net/ and drivers/net/ and is therefore not reached by searches confined to those trees. Target areas: drivers/infiniband (especially ulp/ipoib and core MAD/CMA receive paths), drivers/s390/net (qeth, lcs, ctc), drivers/nfc, drivers/bluetooth (HCI transport packet parsers), drivers/hsi and modem-protocol code under drivers/tty, drivers/isdn, drivers/atm, drivers/staging networking drivers, and any other socket/packet-handling code under drivers/ or elsewhere outside net/ and drivers/net/. In those files hunt all of these: (a) a pointer into the skb linear head (from skb->data, skb->data + off, a cast of skb->data, an skb_header_pointer() return, or skb_network_header()/skb_transport_header() accessors) saved before pskb_may_pull()/pskb_pull() and dereferenced after without refetch; (b) the same staleness across pskb_expand_head(), skb_cow()/skb_cow_head(), skb_linearize(), pskb_trim(), skb_carve(), skb_realloc_headroom(); (c) reads of multi-byte or attacker-length-driven headers at skb->data with no pskb_may_pull/skb_headlen guarantee on a receive path; (d) skb or skb-data pointers used after the skb is freed, handed off via netif_rx()/netif_receive_skb()/skb_queue_tail()/sock_queue_rcv_skb(), or stored into per-device/per-channel/per-firmware private state. Method: grep those directories for pskb_may_pull, pskb_pull, skb_pull, skb_cow, pskb_trim, skb_linearize, skb_header_pointer, kfree_skb and audit each enclosing function plus its callers. Report file:line with the verbatim save, invalidating call, and use lines, and the path by which an attacker-supplied packet reaches the code. Never report net/phonet/pep.c pep_get_sb. Do not use git history, git metadata, or the network.
